subject: Quokka Systems connector issue — response matrix & SLA alignment

Subject: Quokka connector falling behind + logs attached

Hi Marissa —

We started seeing backlog on the Quokka -> Redwood webhook connector last night (Nov 18 ~23:00 UTC). Events are queuing and retries are timing out; this is impacting downstream processing for two pilot customers (EnterpriseCorp, one customer ID included below). I attached a trove of connector logs and a small sample of failing payloads.

We need to align on an escalation path and an SLA-aware response matrix for these kinds of integration degradations. Specifically:
- Expected initial response window for P1 vs P2 (we saw a multi-hour gap)
- Who is primary contact on Redwood side for triage and who should be looped for escalation to infra
- Temporary mitigation steps (rate-limiting, replay window extension) and whether Redwood can enable a retention bump for the queue for 24 hours

Can we set a quick alignment call and draft a short response matrix we can both adopt? Tom Alvarez at EnterpriseCorp is CC'd on this thread and is anxiously awaiting a plan.

Attachments: connector-logs-20261118.zip (6.2MB)

Thanks,

Thanks Ellen — and Tom, sorry you're seeing this. I dug into the initial logs and we can confirm increased retry rates from the connector starting 2026-11-18 22:45 UTC. Early notes: the runtime autoscaler briefly lagged during a burst of long-tail requests and the connector's replay window exhausted for a subset of events.

Proposed immediate actions (short):
- Redwood: open a P1 triage and assign an on-call owner (I'm assigning Sergio for triage ownership).
- Quokka: provide a sanitized sample of the failing payloads (already attached) and confirm whether you want retries extended to 72h for the pilot.
- Joint: 30-min war room call now if available; otherwise tomorrow morning PDT.

I'll draft a simple response matrix (who->what->when) and circulate. Once we have alignment we'll lock a temporary runbook (1–2 weeks) while we implement a longer-term queue/backpressure fix.

Next steps: Sergio will start triage and propose an initial response matrix by EOD tomorrow. Ellen: any constraints re: replay window extension?

Best,

On Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 5:22 PM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll draft a simple response matrix (who->what->when) and circulate.

Quick update from triage: the immediate cause is a combination of (1) an edge-case HTTP 429 loop from a downstream partner that causes repeated retries, and (2) insufficient short-term KV cache for the connector's backoff state, which permits retries to re-enqueue more aggressively than expected. We're not seeing data loss, but the queue depth grew past our typical 2-hour SLA window.

Attached is a one-page draft response matrix (I pasted below) and two mitigation options:

Response matrix (draft):
- P1 (complete outage / data loss risk): initial ack within 15 minutes, on-call engineer assigned within 30 minutes, cross-team page to infra within 60 minutes, mitigation window 4 hours.
- P2 (severe degradation): initial ack within 60 minutes, triage within 4 hours, mitigation window 24 hours.
- P3 (minor / cosmetic): next business day response.

Mitigation options proposed:
A) Short-term: temporarily increase connector retry jitter and extend replay retention to 72h for Quokka pilot only (requires signed consent from Quokka).
B) Medium-term: bump KV cache allocation for connector state (config change, low-risk deploy).

Requesting Quokka decision on option A within 6 hours if you want immediate replay extension. If we get consent we'll also open a temporary config change and document it in the shared Drive link.

Attachments: quokka-response-matrix-v1.xlsx

—
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Integrations Reliability, Redwood Inference

Please keep us posted if there are any impact windows we should avoid (we have nightly batch jobs at 02:00 UTC).

I attached a brief signed consent memo and an inventory of pilot customer IDs (sensitive info redacted). Happy to take the war room call tomorrow morning PDT.

Appreciate the quick sign-off, Ellen — and thank you Rajesh and Tom for patience. TL;DR: we have consensus for the short-term plan and an owner chain. Below is the agreed response matrix and escalation path we will adopt while Redwood implements the medium-term KV allocation change. I'll push a cleaned version to the shared Drive link and loop in CS for customer comms.

Final agreed response matrix (effective immediately)
- P1: initial ack 15m, on-call owner assigned 30m (Sergio), infra escalation 60m (Ben), mitigation window 4 hours.
- P2: ack 60m, triage 4 hours, mitigation 24 hours.
- P3: NBD.

Escalation points and roles
- Triage owner (Redwood): Sergio Alvarez (sergio_alvarez@redwood.com) — responsible for root-cause triage and short-term mitigations.
- Infra escalation (Redwood): Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwood.com) — responsible for infra-level deploys and config changes.
- Partner liaison (Quokka): Ellen Park (ellen.park@quokka.ai) / Rajesh Nair.

Temporary actions taken
- Redwood enabled replay window extension to 72h for the Quokka pilot at 2026-11-21 09:30 PST.
- We scheduled a medium-term config change to bump connector KV allocation on 2026-11-24 02:00 UTC (low-risk).

Related links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_Quokka_ResponseMatrix (clean copy + signed consent)

If there are no objections, we'll treat this as the official SLA addendum for the pilot and roll into the partner onboarding checklist for Quokka's integration work.
